Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to make the amendments that need to be brought to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act) in order to set out the circumstances in which, where MIRA determines the amount of tax payable by taxpayers and the taxpayer objects to the amount so determined and appeals MIRA's decision at the Tax Appeal Tribunal, 100% of the disputed amount out of the amount determined by MIRA must be paid before such an appeal is filed.

Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act)

Bringing the following amendments to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act).

1. Amending subsection (q) of Article 44 of the said Law as follows.

44. (q) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Article, where a taxpayer files a case with the Tax Appeal Tribunal in relation to an amount of tax determined by MIRA under Article 39 of this Law, that case may be appealed at the Tax Appeal Tribunal only after the taxpayer has paid and settled to MIRA an amount equal to at least 50% (fifty percent) of the amount, out of the amount of tax determined by MIRA, that the taxpayer appeals at the Tribunal.

Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to make the amendments required to Law No. 10/2011 (Goods and Services Tax Act) in order to stop the GST that has been levied since 01 October 2026, as part of goods and services of the tourism sector, on inbound tourism products provided by persons without a permanent place of business in the Maldives and on agency or booking services provided in relation to such products, and to further strengthen the measures MIRA can take against persons who engage in GST avoidance.

Disregarding GST avoidance transactions

63-1. (a) If any person carries out, or participates in, a transaction that meets the following conditions, that person shall be deemed to have carried out, or participated in, a GST avoidance transaction.

(1) Any person has obtained a tax benefit from that transaction;

(2) Having regard to the substance of the transaction, it is considered that the sole or main reason for which the person who carried out the transaction or participated in it did so was to facilitate obtaining a tax benefit.

(b) If any person carries out, or participates in, a GST avoidance transaction, the Commissioner General has the discretion to treat that transaction as not having been carried out or participated in, and to determine that the transaction is not an acceptable transaction for tax purposes or to treat it as a void transaction.

(c) For the purpose of this Article, "transaction" means the following matters, and matters done in implementing and carrying out those

(7) Any matter or circumstance that facilitates determining that any goods or service taxable under this Act are goods or a service not taxable under this Act;

(8) Any matter or circumstance that facilitates a person being able to offset an amount against their output tax as input tax, by linking it to an amount paid in selling taxable goods or services and providing other goods or services.

(e) If the Commissioner General decides under (b) of this Article to determine that a GST avoidance transaction is not an acceptable transaction for tax purposes or to treat it as a void transaction, the Commissioner General has the discretion to make changes, affected by the outcome of that transaction, to the amount of tax payable by a registered person, the amount of refund receivable by a registered person, or the amount of input tax deductible by a registered person, in a manner that removes the tax benefit obtained by the registered person as a result of that transaction.

(f) (e) of this Article shall apply to a registered person whether or not that registered person is the person who carried out, or a person who participated in, the GST avoidance transaction specified in this Article.

Bill on the Privileges of Diplomatic Missions, Consular Posts and International Organisations

Chapter One
Introduction and Purpose

Introduction and title
1. (a) This is the Act that sets out the privileges available in the Maldives, in accordance with the international treaties to which the Maldives is a party, to diplomatic missions, consular posts, the specialised agencies of the United Nations and other related bodies, and other international administrative organisations established in the Maldives, and to persons belonging to those establishments.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Diplomatic Missions, Consular Posts and International Organisations (Privileges) Act".

Purpose of the Act
2. The main purpose of this Act is to achieve the following:

(a) to determine, in accordance with the Convention on Diplomatic Relations and the Convention on Consular Relations, the privileges granted to diplomatic missions and consular posts established in the Maldives, to all persons employed at those establishments, and to the members of their families forming part of their households;

[stamp] [signature]

(b) to determine, in accordance with the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the Specialised Agencies of the United Nations, the privileges granted to the specialised agencies, other related bodies and persons belonging to those establishments; and

(c) to determine the privileges granted to the international organisations specifically set out in the Act and to persons connected with those organisations.

Chapter Two
Diplomatic and Consular Relations

Part One - Diplomatic Relations

Implementation of the Convention on Diplomatic Relations
3. (a) The following articles of the Convention on Diplomatic Relations, included in Schedule 1 of this Act, shall have the force of law in the Maldives as set out in Part One of this Chapter:

(1) Article 1 of the Convention;

(2) Articles 22 to 24 of the Convention;

(3) Articles 27 to 40 of the Convention.

(b) For the purposes of the articles of the Convention referred to in subsection (a) of this section, the following expressions and words referred to in that Convention shall have the meanings given to them below.

[stamp] [signature]

(1) "Receiving State" means the Maldives.

(2) "National of the receiving State" means a citizen of the Maldives.

(3) "Agents of the receiving State" as stated in paragraph (1) of Article 22 of the Convention on Diplomatic Relations means a member of the Maldives Police Service and all persons empowered by law to enter premises.

Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to make the amendments that need to be brought to Law No. 24/2020 (Education Act) in order to introduce a home-schooling programme into the said Law, so as to make it possible to provide school education at the home where a child lives on the basis of an assessment made according to the degree of the child's disability or the extent of the child's psychological condition; to set out in the Law the conditions and principles for granting the opportunity to study under that programme; to further detail the role of parents, teachers and principals in running and implementing the school education system; and to resolve other difficulties encountered in implementing the Law.

Reasons for Submitting the Bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this Bill is to guarantee legal protection for the right to protection of name and reputation afforded to every person under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives; to establish an appropriate balance between the right to freedom of expression in society and the protection and preservation of the reputation of individuals; to state that a party who has been defamed has the right to have the truth of the matter disclosed, or to reply, or to have the matter corrected; and, in addition, to determine that defamation is a civil wrong, to set out what constitutes defamation, the circumstances that shall not be deemed defamation and the circumstances in which privilege is afforded, and to set out all the principles and standards for seeking an apology from the party who defames, for making an offer of compensation, for a defamed party to file a case in court to seek compensation for the damage suffered, and for the award of compensation for damage.

Introduction and Title
1. (a) This is an Act to set out, in a manner by which the right to have one's name and reputation protected, afforded to every person under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, can be enforced in practice, the legal protection to be afforded under that right; to set out the standard for determining defamation and the circumstances that shall not be deemed defamation; to determine that defamation is a civil wrong; and to set out the legal remedies available to a defamed party as a result of defamation and all other related principles.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Right to Protection of Name and Reputation Act".

Purpose
2. The purpose of this Act is to achieve the following.

(a) Whereas the right of persons to have their name and reputation protected is guaranteed under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, to take legal measures in order not to allow that right to be

(b) This Act shall apply to all of the following productions.

(1) Statements made in writing or orally, and statements made in visual and/or audio form;

(2) Material of every kind that is broadcast, printed or published online;

(3) Any other means by which a statement is made or disseminated in a manner that communicates it to, or allows it to reach, any third party.

(c) This Act shall not apply to a private communication between two parties, if that communication was held solely in a private manner and is not disclosed to any third party. However, if such a communication reaches or is disseminated to any third party or the public by any means, that communication shall fall within the scope of this Act.

(d) This Act shall apply to all of the following acts.

(1) All acts of defamation committed within the territory of the Maldives; and

(2) All acts of defamation committed outside the territory of the Maldives

in the following circumstances.

i. The defamatory statement being available in the Maldives; and

ii. It being deemed, on the basis of reasonable grounds, that as a result thereof the reputation of a party in the Maldives has been damaged or may be damaged.

(e) Even if an act specified in subsection (d) of this Article was committed wholly or to any extent outside the territory of the Maldives, the courts of the Maldives shall have jurisdiction over such acts.

Chapter Two
Right to Protection of Name and Reputation

Scope of the Right to Protection of Name and Reputation
5. (a) Every person has the right to legal protection against unlawful attacks on that person's name and reputation. And every person has the right to seek compensation for damage suffered as a result of defamation.

(b) If damage is caused to the name and reputation of any person by an act committed unlawfully or by negligence, the State shall establish, in accordance with this Act, an easily accessible system through which appropriate legal remedies may be obtained.

[stamp] [signature]

(c) In exercising the right to protection of name and reputation, that right shall not be interpreted or applied in a manner that restricts lawful expression, debate and criticism to an unreasonable extent.

Duty to Respect the Rights of Others
6. (a) Every person shall exercise the freedom of expression afforded to him under Article 27 of the Constitution in accordance with Article 67 of the Constitution, in a responsible manner, safeguarding the rights, freedoms and reputation of others, and with full respect for those rights, freedoms and reputation.

(b) The media, digital platforms and other parties engaged in the work of publication shall maintain a standard of reasonable care in order to ensure the accuracy, fairness and credibility of the information disseminated through their platforms.

(c) The media, digital platforms and other parties engaged in the work of publication shall establish and implement appropriate mechanisms for promptly correcting, clarifying or withdrawing information provided by them, if it becomes known that such information is false or misleading.

(d) By acting in accordance with this Article, that party being deemed to be absolved from a responsibility imposed upon any person or party under other Articles of this Act

[stamp] [signature]

shall not be permitted.

Right of Reply
7. A defamed party has the right to have the truth of the defamatory matter disclosed, or to reply to it, or to have the matter corrected.

Chapter Three
Defamation

Determination of the Wrong
8. Defamation is a civil wrong. And every party defamed as a result of defamation has the right to seek and obtain the solutions or remedies determined in this Act.

Defamation
9. In this Act, "defamation" means the commission by another party, intentionally or without reasonable care, against a particular party or in relation to a particular party, of an act among the following acts.

(a) Attributing a false statement to a particular party, or giving or publishing false information, or committing an act by which false information is obtained; and

(b) As a result of making that false statement, or giving or publishing false information, or committing an act by which that information is obtained, an adverse change occurring in the respect shown towards, or in the regard held of, the party to whom that statement or information was attributed in the minds of right-thinking members of society; or hatred towards that party being brought about; or, as a result of that statement or of what was published,

[stamp] [signature]

(5) Through objects made in the form of something attributable to a particular person or in a manner depicting a person, or by a film made, or through things such as stage shows and dramatic performances; or

(6) Something defamatory of a particular party coming to be portrayed, conceived, understood or known as a result of gestures made, movements made or any other act committed.

(b) If, through an act specified in subsection (a) of this Article, the reputation of a person is impugned, whether directly and explicitly or indirectly, it shall be deemed defamation for the purposes of this Act.

Standard for Determining Defamation
11. (a) For the purposes of this Act, a particular party shall be deemed to have been defamed if the following conditions are fulfilled in relation to an act specified in Article 10 of this Act.

(1) The statement made or the information given being a false statement or false information;

(2) The statement made or the information given being something that has been made public;

(3) The statement made or the information given being a statement or information attributable to the defamed party.

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a)(1) of this Article, however damaging the statement

[stamp] [signature]

or the information given may be to the reputation of the defamed party, if it is true, it shall not be deemed an act of defamation.

(c) For the purposes of subsection (a)(2) of this Article, the following principles shall apply in determining whether a statement made or information given has been made public.

(1) If it is proven that the statement made or the information given was not a statement made or information given with the intention of making it public, that statement or information shall not be deemed to have been made public.

(2) Notwithstanding subsection (c)(1) of this Article, if it is reasonable to believe that the statement or information may reach a third party, that statement or information shall be deemed to have been made public. Accordingly, a statement or information shall be deemed to have been made public in the following circumstances.

i. The statement having been made or the information having been given to, or in the presence of, a third party other than the defamed party; or

ii. The statement or the information given being a writing, statement, photograph, video, song or other information published in a book, newspaper or magazine, or broadcast through radio, television

[stamp] [signature]

to believe, from the words or information used, that it refers to the defamed party, that statement or information shall be deemed to be attributable to the defamed party.

(b) The party who wrote, published or disclosed a defamatory thing specified in subsection (a) of this Article, or parties who disseminate such a thing to further parties, shall bear responsibility for it under this Act. (c) For the purposes of this Article, internet service providers shall not be required to bear responsibility under this Act.

read through the internet in the Maldives; or

(2) The defamed party being a Maldivian citizen, or a party residing or established in the Maldives.

(b) The statement made or the information given in attribution to a person being an opinion or view based on the true facts.

Bringing a Defamation Action

Chapter One
Preliminary

Introduction and title
1. (a) This is the Act that determines the conditions that must be fulfilled for the death penalty to be determined upon persons in the Maldives and the principles that courts must follow in determining the penalty, and sets out the procedures that must be completed in sequence for the enforcement of the death penalty, the rights to be afforded to the person upon whom the death penalty has been determined, the circumstances and reasons for which the enforcement of the penalty shall be postponed, and finally, the principles and procedures relating to the determination of the death penalty and the enforcement of the penalty.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Death Penalty Determination and Enforcement Act".

Purpose
2. The purpose of this Act is to achieve the following:

(a) to determine the conditions that must be fulfilled for the death penalty to be determined upon a person, where a court of the Maldives has proven upon that person an offence for which the death penalty may be determined;

[stamp] [signature]

the penalty carried out where, at the trial of a criminal case conducted in a court of the Maldives, the offence is proven against the party accused of the offence, and the court sentences that person to be put to death as a penalty for that offence.

Chapter Two
Conditions for Determining the Death Penalty

Not determining the penalty unless the conditions for the death penalty are fulfilled
5. No court of the Maldives shall determine the death penalty upon any person unless all the conditions set out in this Chapter are fulfilled, and only in accordance with the procedures set out in this Chapter.

Determination of the penalty by law
6. (a) In determining the death penalty upon the convicted person, in addition to the offence proven against that person being determined and set out as a hadd offence in Law No. 9/2014 (Penal Code of the Maldives) or in another Act specifically designated for determining criminal offences and penalties, it must be stated in that Act that the penalty for that offence, or a penalty among the penalties for it, is the death penalty.

(b) The condition set out in subsection (a) of this Article must have been fulfilled in that court from the time the convicted person committed the offence until the sentence determining the death penalty upon that person is passed.

7. (a) Even where a lower court has sentenced the convicted person to death as a penalty for the offence, all the legal points of that sentence and the facts of the case shall be

[stamp] [signature]

(b) Even where neither the State nor the convicted person submits the case for appeal to a superior court, the superior courts shall hear that case as an appeal case in the manner set out in subsection (a) of this Article.

(c) A sentence determining the death penalty shall become a final sentence only when, after the Supreme Court has heard that case, that Court determines the death penalty upon the convicted person.

8. (a) The death penalty shall be determined upon the convicted person only after a trial conducted with fairness and justice, impartially and equitably, at a hearing held open to the public, within a reasonable period, in an independent and [unclear] court guaranteed by law.

(b) Before the Supreme Court determines the death penalty upon the convicted person, that Court shall ensure that the stages of trial have been conducted in the manner set out in subsection (a) of this Article.

(c) The Supreme Court shall examine whether the matters set out in subsection (a) of this Article have been fulfilled to a standard higher than the standard at which such matters are ordinarily examined, and [unclear] at every stage of the trial.

(d) In examining whether the matters set out in subsection (a) of this Article have been fulfilled, the Supreme Court shall examine them in a manner that includes the following fundamental matters:

(1) that the right set out in Article 42 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person;

(2) that the right set out in Article 51 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person;

(3) that the right set out in Article 56 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person.
